headline: OSISKO DEVELOPMENT APPROVES $990M CARIBOO CONSTRUCTION — FIRST BC GOLD POUR Q1 2029, 22% COMPLETE NOW
snippet: Osisko Development Corp (TSX: ODV) formally committed to construction of its 100%-owned Cariboo Gold Project in central British Columbia — a decade of de-risking since 2015 culminating in a $990M go-forward capital obligation supported by $837M cash on hand and up to $1.637B in total available financing. With detailed engineering 40% complete, long-lead procurement 44% committed, and the project 22% complete as of July 31, the mine targets first gold pour in Q1 2029 and commercial production within 36 months; it will sustain approximately 525 permanent jobs in BC.

headline: 63 MINING PROJECTS HEADLINE CANADA'S C$1 TRILLION INVESTMENT SUMMIT — CARNEY WOOS BLACKROCK, NORWAY SOVEREIGN FUND
snippet: Prime Minister Mark Carney's inaugural Canada Investment Summit (Sept 14–15, Toronto) lists 63 mining projects among 167 investment opportunities pitched to 100 global investors managing $70+ trillion in assets — including BlackRock's Larry Fink, Norway's Government Pension Fund, and Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. Mining commands more than a third of the C$1 trillion five-year investment target, with projects ranging from Troilus Mining's $1.43B Quebec gold-copper build to junior explorers seeking first institutional capital; BMO says the combination of critical-mineral demand, government incentives, and expanding development spending makes Canada uniquely positioned.

headline: HERCULES METALS DRILLS EDGE OF 1.8KM HOOK ANOMALY — NEW PORPHYRY CENTRE EXPANDS IDAHO COPPER DISTRICT
snippet: Hercules Metals (TSX-V: BIG / OTC: BADEF) announced hole HER-26-03 intersected intense quartz-sericite-pyrite phyllic alteration and distal skarn in calcareous hosts at the Hook target on its Idaho property — alteration consistent with the outer edge of a porphyry copper system, located 3 km east of the producing Leviathan porphyry. A ~1.8 km chargeability anomaly has its high-strength core modelled within approximately 100 metres of surface; drill permitting for core hole access roads and pads is underway with the follow-up drill program targeting 2027.

headline: NEXGOLD GOLDBORO IN FEDERAL PITCHBOOK — 2.58MOZ AT 3.72 G/T NOVA SCOTIA GOLD, 100KOZ/YEAR FORECAST
snippet: NexGold Mining (TSX-V: NEXG) confirmed its fully permitted Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia was selected for the Canada Investment Summit Prospectus — the government's pitchbook distributed to global institutional investors at today's Toronto summit. The feasibility study projects 100,000 oz/year average gold production over a 10.9-year mine life from 2.58 million ounces M&I at a high-grade 3.72 g/t; an updated resource estimate and 40,000-metre infill drill program are underway, with a construction decision anticipated in 2026.

headline: GOLDGROUP UPSIZES PLACEMENT TO US$125M — TRAFIGURA, ERIC SPROTT AND RICK RULE BACK MEXICAN GOLD MINER
snippet: Goldgroup Mining (TSX-V: GORO / NYSE American: GORO) upsized its private placement from US$75M to US$125M after strong institutional demand, with approximately $60M already committed by entities affiliated with Trafigura, Eric Sprott, Rick Rule, Fiscal Wisdom, and Calu Opportunity Fund. Proceeds will advance the Don David Gold Mine (Oaxaca), Cerro Prieto Gold Mine (Sonora), the San Francisco Gold Project, and the Back Forty Project (Michigan); closing is expected on or about September 30, 2026, pending TSX-V conditional approval.

headline: CHINA DOUBLES LITHIUM STOCKPILE COUNT TO 175,000T — CARBONATE CRATERS 14% IN 3 SESSIONS, MARKET IN DATA CRISIS
snippet: A September 8 methodology change at data provider SMM (Shanghai Metals Market) doubled China's reported lithium carbonate stockpiles overnight from 78,800 to 175,000 tonnes, triggering a 14% crash in futures over three sessions to approximately US$20,100/tonne. As of Monday September 14, lithium carbonate sits at CNY 138,650/t, down another 2.53%, as the sector debates whether the inventory figure reflects true oversupply or a data artefact; China's largest lithium producers are calling for standardized third-party data methodology after the price chaos.

headline: NEW MEXICO BANS NEW URANIUM MINING ON 13M+ STATE ACRES — RESISTANCE MOVEMENT COUNTERS TRUMP EXPANSION PUSH
snippet: New Mexico Land Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard's executive order banning new uranium mining leases on 13 million-plus acres of state trust land is now the centrepiece of a growing resistance movement covered in depth in a September 14 CounterPunch analysis. New Mexico has more than 1,000 former uranium mining sites and 250 abandoned contaminated areas — its history as the U.S.'s former top uranium producer fuelling scepticism of the Trump administration's push for new domestic production; the ban does not affect the state's two existing active leases or federal lands within New Mexico.

headline: GOLDSEEK: HOT CPI DATA AND SAUDI OIL SHOCK CREATE BUY ZONES FOR MINING STOCKS AHEAD OF FED BINARY
snippet: GoldSeek's September 13 analysis argues the August CPI print (+0.4% MoM, +3.4% YoY) and Monday's Saudi oil shock — which hardened rate-hike bets to ~87% — have created a historically reliable entry zone for gold mining stocks ahead of this week's FOMC meeting. With gold pulled back from the $4,691 August high to $4,285 and junior miners down 2–3x gold's percentage move, the article identifies specific technical and fundamental buy zones, noting that similar macro setups in the prior cycle preceded the sector's strongest multi-month advances.

headline: RECORD $2,300/OZ MINER MARGINS NOT PRICED IN — WHY GOLD EQUITY LEVERAGE HAS BROKEN DOWN AT $4,285 GOLD
snippet: With gold at $4,285 and industry all-in sustaining costs averaging below $2,000/oz, gold producers are generating record per-ounce cash margins — yet the historical 2–4x leverage ratio of miner stocks to the metal appears broken, with GDXJ falling harder than gold on every corrective move. GoldSilver.com's September analysis examines why unprecedented margin levels haven't triggered a re-rating, pointing to institutional memory of the 2011–2015 miner collapse, energy-cost uncertainty from $108 oil, and the market's structural preference for physical gold over producer equity exposure.
